By any other name would smell as sweet;
So Romeo would, were he not Romeo call’d,
Retain that dear perfection which he owes
Without that title.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: In all times, either men have spoken of the true God, or the true God has spoken to men.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: Courage is resistance to fear, mastery of fear--not absence of fear.
quotes.author: Mark Twain

quotes.text: The justest man in the world is not allowed to be judge in his own cause; I know some who, in order not to fall into this self-love, have been perfectly unjust out of opposition.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: Six years Already have I reigned in peace; but joy Dwells not within my soul.
quotes.author: Alexander Pushkin

quotes.text: You have two things to lose, the true and the good; and two things to stake, your reason and your will, your knowledge and your happiness; and your nature has two things to shun, error and misery.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text:
Not on the lips of men Love’s secret lies,
Remote and unrevealed his dwelling-place.
Oh Saki, come! the idle laughter dies
When thou the feast with heavenly wine dost grace.
Patience and wisdom, Hafiz, in a sea
Of thine own tears are drowned; thy misery
They could not still nor hide from curious eyes.
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: Men will never believe with a saving and real faith, unless God inclines their heart; and they will believe as soon as He inclines it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: The soul unfolds itself, like a lotus of countless petals.
quotes.author: Kahlil Gibran

quotes.text: The conduct of God, who disposes all things kindly, is to put religion into the mind by reason, and into the heart by grace.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: God grows weary of great kingdoms, but never of little flowers.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: The easiest conditions to live in according to the world are the most difficult to live in according to God, and vice versa.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: Do not confuse opinions with certainties.
quotes.author: Arabic proverb

quotes.text: Nothing is so difficult according to the world as the religious life; nothing is easier than to live it according to God.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text:
Parting is such sweet sorrow
That I shall say good night till it be morrow.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Truth is so obscure in these times, and falsehood so established, that unless we love the truth, we cannot know it.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text:
This is my letter to the world,
That never wrote to me, --
The simple news that Nature told,
With tender majesty.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: All I know is that I must soon die, but what I know least is this very death which I cannot escape.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: I thought To satisfy my people in contentment, In glory, gain their love by generous gifts, But I have put away that empty hope; The power that lives is hateful to the mob,-- Only the dead they love.
quotes.author: Alexander Pushkin

quotes.text: The strength of a man's virtue must not be measured by his efforts, but by his ordinary life.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text:
To them that here renowned for virtue live,
A heavenly palace is the meet reward;
To me, the drunkard and the beggar, give
The temple of the grape with red wine stored!
Beside a river seat thee on the sward;
It floweth past—so flows thy life away,
So sweetly, swiftly, fleets our little day—
Swift, but enough for me!
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: We cannot but desire truth and happiness, and are incapable of certainty or happiness.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: Wrong cannot afford defeat but Right can.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Man is to himself the most wonderful object in nature; for he cannot conceive what the body is, still less what the mind is, and least of all how a body should be united to a mind.
quotes.author: Blaise Pascal

quotes.text: He who thinks well of others is a happy man.
quotes.author: Arabic proverb

quotes.text: We may make an oratory of our heart so we can, from time to time, retire to converse with Him in meekness, humility, and love.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
These violent delights have violent ends,
And in their triumph die; like fire and powder,
Which as they kiss consume.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: We ought not weary of doing little things for the love of God, who regards not the greatness of the work, but the love with which it is performed.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Success is counted sweetest
By those who ne'er succeed.
To comprehend a nectar
Requires sorest need.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: We ought to love our friends, but without encroaching upon the love of God, which must always be first.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: We are but fools When our heart vibrates to the people's groans And passionate wailing.
quotes.author: Alexander Pushkin

quotes.text: Ever since that time I walk before God simply, in faith, with humility, and with love.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Except thy road through affliction pass,
None may reach the halting-station of mirth;
God’s treaty: Am I not Lord of the earth?
Man sealed with a sigh: Ah yes, alas!
Nor with Is nor Is Not let thy mind contend;
Rest assured all perfection of mortal birth
In the great Is Not at the last shall end.
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: If our love of God were great we would love Him equally in pain and pleasure.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: Every child comes with the message that God is not yet discouraged of man.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: We cannot have too much trust in so good and faithful a Friend who will never fail us in this world nor in the next.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
For aught that I could ever read,
Could ever hear by tale or history,
The course of true love never did run smooth.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: At those times I did not pray for any relief, but I prayed for strength to suffer with courage, humility, and love.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
If I can stop one heart from breaking,
I shall not live in vain;
If I can ease one life the aching,
Or cool one pain,
Or help one fainting robin
Unto his nest again,
I shall not live in vain.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: If, in this life, we might enjoy the peace of paradise, we must accustom ourselves to a familiar, humble, and affectionate conversation with God.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Mirth, Spring, to linger in a garden fair,
What more has earth to give? All ye that wait,
Where is the Cup-bearer, the flagon where?
When pleasant hours slip from the hand of Fate,
Reckon each hour as a certain gain;
Who seeks to know the end of mortal care
Shall question his experience in vain.
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: We must work faithfully without trouble or disquiet, recalling our mind to God mildly and with tranquillity as often as we find it wandering from Him.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: We are as strictly obliged to adhere to God by action in the time of action, as by prayer in its season.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind;
And therefore is wing’d Cupid painted blind.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: We need only to recognize God intimately present with us and address ourselves to Him every moment.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
A wounded deer leaps highest,
I've heard the hunter tell;
'T is but the ecstasy of death,
And then the brake is still.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: Gradually become accustomed to worship Him in this way; to beg His grace, to offer Him your heart from time to time; in the midst of your business, even every moment if you can.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Consider the rose that breaks into flower,
Neither repines though she fade and die—
The powers of the world endure for an hour,
But nought shall remain of their majesty.
Be not too sure of your crown, you who thought
That virtue was easy and recompense yours;
From the monastery to the wine-tavern doors
The way is nought!
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: Please keep my recommendation in mind that you think of God often; by day, by night, in your business, and even in your diversions.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: He who wants to do good knocks at the gate; he who loves finds the gate open.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Let us often consider that our only business in this life is to please God, that perhaps all besides is but folly and vanity.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: Nothing will come of nothing: speak again.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: One way to re-collect the mind easily in the time of prayer, and preserve it more in tranquillity, is not to let it wander too far at other times.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Much madness is divinest sense
To a discerning eye;
Much sense the starkest madness.
'T is the majority
In this, as all, prevails.
Assent, and you are sane;
Demur, -- you're straightway dangerous,
And handled with a chain.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: We cannot escape the dangers which abound in life without the actual and continual help of God.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text:
Lay not reproach at the drunkard’s door
Oh Fanatic, thou that art pure of soul;
Not thine on the page of life to enrol
The faults of others! Or less or more
I have swerved from my path—keep thou to thine own!
For every man when he reaches the goal
Shall reap the harvest his hands have sown.
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: Whether God led us by suffering or by consolation all would be equal to a soul truly resigned.
quotes.author: Brother Lawrence
quotes.work: The Practice of the Presence of God

quotes.text: Death's stamp gives value to the coin of life; making it possible to buy with life what is truly precious.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: The point is not that this world is too sad to love or too glad not to love; the point is that when you do love a thing, its gladness is a reason for loving it, and its sadness a reason for loving it more.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
How sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is
To have a thankless child!
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: It is all the difference between being free from them, as a man is free from a prison, and being free of them as a man is free of a city.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
The soul selects her own society,
Then shuts the door;
On her divine majority
Obtrude no more.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: No one doubts that an ordinary man can get on with this world: but we demand not strength enough to get on with it, but strength enough to get it on.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Ah, seek the treasure of a mind at rest
And store it in the treasury of Ease;
Not worth a loyal heart, a tranquil breast,
Were all the riches of thy lands and seas!
Ah, scorn, like Hafiz, the delights of earth,
Ask not one grain of favour from the base,
Two hundred sacks of jewels were not worth
Thy soul’s disgrace!
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: Man must have just enough faith in himself to have adventures, and just enough doubt of himself to enjoy them.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text: Do not linger to gather flowers to keep them, but walk on, for flowers will keep themselves blooming all your way.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: Man is more himself, man is more manlike, when joy is the fundamental thing in him, and grief the superficial.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
We are such stuff
As dreams are made on, and our little life
Is rounded with a sleep.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: The truth is that there is a real humility typical of our time; but it so happens that it is practically a more poisonous humility than the wildest prostrations of the ascetic.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
To fight aloud is very brave,
But gallanter, I know,
Who charge within the bosom,
The cavalry of woe.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: The modern world is not evil; in some ways the modern world is far too good.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
The modest and the merry shall be seen
To boast their kinship with a single voice;
There are no differences to choose between,
Thou art but flattering thy soul with choice!
Who knows the Curtain’s secret?... Heaven is mute!
And yet with Him who holds the Curtain, e’en
With Him, oh Braggart, thou would’st raise dispute!
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: He must seek his life in a spirit of furious indifference to it; he must desire life like water and yet drink death like wine.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text: Do not insult your friend by lending him merits from your own pocket.
quotes.author: Rabindranath Tagore

quotes.text: We do not want joy and anger to neutralize each other and produce a surly contentment; we want a fiercer delight and a fiercer discontent.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
What’s past is prologue, what to come
In yours and my discharge.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: A man may be said loosely to love himself, but he can hardly fall in love with himself, or, if he does, it must be a monotonous courtship.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Pain has an element of blank;
It cannot recollect
When it began, or if there were
A day when it was not.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: It is absurd to say that you are especially advancing freedom when you only use free thought to destroy free will.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Heaven’s garden future treasures may yield—
Ah, make the most of earth’s treasury!
The flickering shade of the willow-tree,
And the grass-grown lip of the fruitful field.
Trust not in deeds—the Eternal Day
Shall reveal the Creator’s sentence on thee;
But till then, what His finger has writ, who can say.
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: A soldier surrounded by enemies, if he is to cut his way out, needs to combine a strong desire for living with a strange carelessness about dying.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Do not go to the garden of flowers!
O Friend! go not there;
In your body is the garden of flowers.
Take your seat on the thousand petals of the lotus, and there gaze on the Infinite Beauty.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: The man who is most likely to ruin the place he loves is exactly the man who loves it with a reason.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text: Who steals my purse steals trash.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: It is the happy man who does the useless things; the sick man is not strong enough to be idle.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
I had no time to hate, because
The grave would hinder me,
And life was not so ample I
Could finish enmity.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: I had found this hole in the world: the fact that one must somehow find a way of loving the world without trusting it; somehow one must love the world without being worldly.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Not all the sum of earthly happiness
Is worth the bowed head of a moment’s pain,
And if I sell for wine my dervish dress,
Worth more than what I sell is what I gain!
Land where my Lady dwells, thou holdest me
Enchained; else Fars were but a barren soil,
Not worth the journey over land and sea,
Not worth the toil!
quotes.author: Hafez

quotes.text: It is simple about the simple truth; but it is stubborn about the subtle truth.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
The moon shines in my body, but my blind eyes cannot see it:
The moon is within me, and so is the sun.
The unstruck drum of Eternity is sounded within me; but my deaf ears cannot hear it.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: The moment you step into the world of facts, you step into a world of limits.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton
William Shakespeare

quotes.text: The man who will improve the place is the man who loves it without a reason.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
Nor had I time to love; but since
Some industry must be,
The little toil of love, I thought,
Was large enough for me.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: It means a strong desire to live taking the form of a readiness to die.
quotes.author: G. K. Chesterton

quotes.text:
I am silent. Speak Thou, O Soul of Soul of Soul,
From desire of whose Face every atom grew articulate.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: Were I to live my life over again, I should live it just as I have lived it; I neither complain of the past, nor do I fear the future; and if I am not much deceived, I am the same within that I am without.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
So long as man clamours for the I and the Mine, his works are as naught:
When all love of the I and the Mine is dead, then the work of the Lord is done.
For work has no other aim than the getting of knowledge:
When that comes, then work is put away.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: As if good fortune were a thing inconsistent with good conscience, men never grow good but in evil fortune.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text: Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Whoever saw old age that did not applaud the past and condemn the present time, laying the fault of his misery and discontent upon the world and the manners of men?
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Elysium is as far as to
The very nearest room,
If in that room a friend await
Felicity or doom.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: All the whole time you live, you purloin from life and live at the expense of life itself.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Every moment the voice of Love is coming from left and right.
We are bound for heaven: who has a mind to sight-seeing?
We have been in heaven, we have been friends of the angels;
Thither, Sire, let us return, for that is our country.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: Life in itself is neither good nor evil; it is the scene of good or evil as you make it.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
The river and its waves are one surf: where is the difference between the river and its waves?
When the wave rises, it is the water; and when it falls, it is the same water again.  Tell me, Sir, where is the distinction?
Because it has been named as wave, shall it no longer be considered as water?
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: I always interpret the death by the life preceding; and if any one tell me of a death strong and constant in appearance, annexed to a feeble life, I conclude it produced by some feeble cause, and suitable to the life before.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text: The better part of valour is discretion, in the which better part I have saved my life.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: A man whose morals are good may have false opinions, and a wicked man may preach truth, even though he believe it not himself.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
What fortitude the soul contains,
That it can so endure
The accent of a coming foot,
The opening of a door!
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: The utility of living consists not in the length of days, but in the use of time; a man may have lived long, and yet lived but a little.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Beware! do not keep, in a circle of reprobates,
Thine eye shut like a bud, thy mouth open like the rose.
The world resembles a mirror: thy Love is the perfect image:
O people, who has ever seen a part greater than the whole?
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: The confidence in another man’s virtue is no light evidence of a man’s own, and God willingly favours such a confidence.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Lamps burn in every house, O blind one! and you cannot see them.
One day your eyes shall suddenly be opened, and you shall see: and the fetters of death will fall from you.
There is nothing to say or to hear, there is nothing to do: it is he who is living, yet dead, who shall never die again.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: He who has neither the courage to die nor the heart to live, who will neither resist nor fly, what can we do with him?
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Our doubts are traitors,
And make us lose the good we oft might win
By fearing to attempt.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Pain, pleasure, love and hatred are the first things that a child is sensible of: if, when reason comes, they apply it to themselves, that is virtue.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Here a star, and there a star,
Some lose their way.
Here a mist, and there a mist,
Afterwards -- day!
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: We trouble life by the care of death, and death by the care of life: the one torments, the other frights us.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Be silent that the Lord who gave thee language may speak,
For as He fashioned a door and lock, He has also made a key.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: If I were a writer of books, I would compile a register, with a comment, of the various deaths of men: he who should teach men to die would at the same time teach them to live.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
The lock of error shuts the gate, open it with the key of love:
Thus, by opening the door, thou shalt wake the Beloved.
Kabîr says: "O brother!  do not pass by such good fortune as this."
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: A man may both be too much in love with virtue, and be excessive in a just action.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Love all, trust a few,
Do wrong to none.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: If we have not known how to live, ‘tis injustice to teach us how to die, and make the end difform from all the rest; if we have known how to live firmly and quietly, we shall know how to die so too.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne
Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: A generous heart ought not to belie its own thoughts; it will make itself seen within; all there is good, or at least human.
quotes.author: Michel de Montaigne

quotes.text:
Love is the astrolabe of God's mysteries.
A lover may hanker after this love or that love,
But at the last he is drawn to the KING of Love.
However much we describe and explain Love,
When we fall in love we are ashamed of our words.
Explanation by the tongue makes most things clear,
But Love unexplained is better.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: Crafty men contemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by observation.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
I laugh when I hear that the fish in the water is thirsty:
You do not see that the Real is in your home, and you wander from forest to forest listlessly!
Here is the truth!  Go where you will, to Benares or to Mathura; if you do not find your soul, the world is unreal to you.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: The desire of power in excess, caused the angels to fall; the desire of knowledge in excess, caused man to fall: but in charity there is no excess; neither can angel, nor man, come in danger by it.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer’s lease hath all too short a date:
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Men fear death, as children fear to go in the dark; and as that natural fear in children, is increased with tales, so is the other.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
Alter? When the hills do.
Falter? When the sun
Question if his glory
Be the perfect one.
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: Neither is there only a habit of goodness, directed by right reason; but there is in some men, even in nature, a disposition towards it; as on the other side, there is a natural malignity.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
Whoso recognises and confesses his own defects
Is hastening in the way that leads to Perfection!
But he advances not towards the Almighty
Who fancies himself to be perfect.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: It is true, that a little philosophy inclineth man's mind to atheism; but depth in philosophy bringeth men's minds about to religion.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
Subtle is the path of love!
Therein there is no asking and no not-asking,
There one loses one's self at His feet,
There one is immersed in the joy of the seeking: plunged in the deeps of love as the fish in the water.
The lover is never slow in offering his head for his Lord's service.
Kabîr declares the secret of this love.
quotes.author: Kabir

quotes.text: The virtue of prosperity, is temperance; the virtue of adversity, is fortitude; which in morals is the more heroical virtue.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
So long as men can breathe or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
quotes.author: William Shakespeare

quotes.text: Divide with reason; between self-love and society; and be so true to thyself, as thou be not false to others; specially to thy king and country.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
Have you got a brook in your little heart,
Where bashful flowers blow,
And blushing birds go down to drink,
And shadows tremble so?
quotes.author: Emily Dickinson

quotes.text: Merit and good works, is the end of man's motion; and conscience of the same is the accomplishment of man's rest.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
The sect of lovers is distinct from all others,
Lovers have a religion and a faith of their own.
Though the ruby has no stamp, what matters it?
Love is fearless in the midst of the sea of fear.
quotes.author: Rumi

quotes.text: A man hath a body, and that body is confined to a place; but where friendship is, all offices of life are as it were granted to him, and his deputy.
quotes.author: Francis Bacon

quotes.text:
The flower blooms for the fruit: when the fruit comes, the flower withers.
